title: Calibration-aware, Reference-less & Task-aware Metric Adapter for Quantized Model Validation
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: We need a robust scoring layer for validating quantized model variants (FP8/INT8) that goes beyond simple token-level comparisons. Current pipelines compute isolated metrics (perplexity, accuracy on MMLU-style suites, ROUGE/BLEU) but do not: 1) account for calibration shifts introduced by quantization, 2) operate in reference-less modes for conversational and generative tasks, or 3) attribute task-level signal back to model/component-level decisions for gating and rollouts.

Goal: Implement a metric adapter that: (a) normalizes scores with calibration-aware adjustments (logit temperature scaling / bias correction) so perplexity and confidence-based metrics are comparable across quant profiles; (b) supports both reference-based (ROUGE/BLEU, exact-match, MMLU-style multiple-choice) and reference-less estimators (certainty-based heuristics, learned quality regressors) for tasks with no gold references; (c) produces structured outputs consumable by the Console and the Quality gating system (per-route score breakdown, calibrated confidence, task attribution, regression flags).

Scope: Adapter service + evaluation harness glue code + integration tests + dashboard contract. This ticket focuses on the adapter and core metric implementations; dataset curation and large-scale runs are tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Adapter exposes a stable API to eval harness and runtime that returns: calibrated_perplexity, calibrated_confidence, task_accuracy, rouge_f1, bleu_bleu, reference_less_score (when applicable), and per-task attribution tags; 2) Calibration step documented and reproducible (script + seed) that reports pre/post calibration deltas for a sample benchmark; 3) Unit tests cover edge cases: degenerate logits, very short sequences, all-UNK outputs; 4) Integration smoke test with quant-profiles CI (runs on a small FP8 and INT8 checkpoint) showing metrics reported to Console-compatible JSON with schema v1; 5) PRs reviewed by ML metrics and Runtime owners and merged with CI green.
design_notes:
High-level approach: compute raw metrics as usual, then apply a calibration layer before final aggregation. Calibration options: (A) temperature scaling on logits for perplexity/confidence; (B) additive bias correction learned on a held-out calibration set; (C) Brier score reweighting for probabilistic tasks. For MMLU-style multiple-choice, compute both top-1 accuracy and calibrated soft accuracy (weighted by calibrated probabilities). For reference-less tasks (dialog/chat/code generation), implement a hybrid estimator: heuristics (length/entropy/sequence repetition), embedding-similarity to prompt completions, and a small supervised regressor trained on human labels (features: normalized perplexity, self-BLEU, response length, toxic score). Aggregation: per-task weighted mean with configurable task weights from project config. Outputs: flat JSON with fields required by Console: model, quant_profile, dataset, seed, metrics (list of name/value/unit), attribution (list of tags), calibration_metadata (method, params, calibration_set_id). API: evaluate(adapter_payload) -> adapters/result.json
Implementation details: keep adapter pure Python with a thin Rust-backed scoring primitive for n-gram ROUGE/BLEU to keep latency low. Reuse existing tokenization and logit pipelines from runtime-1.18; ensure compatibility with further runtime releases. Persist calibration artifacts to S3 path and reference them by id in outputs.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype calibration functions and unit tests (2 days); 2) Implement MMLU-style scoring with calibrated soft accuracy (3 days); 3) Implement ROUGE/BLEU via Rust primitive bindings + wrapper (3 days); 4) Build reference-less estimator and train tiny regressor (4 days); 5) Integration layer with eval harness + Console JSON contract (2 days); 6) End-to-end smoke runs on FP8/INT8 model snapshots and iterate (4 days); 7) PR review/merge and docs (2 days). Note: some steps run in parallel: ROUGE primitive and MMLU scorer can be developed concurrently.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration dataset mismatch causing worse apparent scores after calibration. Mitigation: provide explicit pre/post calibration diffs and allow opt-out for rollouts. Risk: Reference-less regressor overfits to small annotation set. Mitigation: keep regressor small, use cross-validation and conservative thresholds; label more examples if needed. Risk: Metric mismatch across runtimes. Mitigation: pin tokenizers and logit processing codepaths; include exact seed and env in outputs.
